turns.prompt_text: I'm scanning a bunch of documents using a Brother printer, and it's going to my Mac Mini. My Mac Mini has Color Sync Utility open; however, I'm not sure where it's saving to.
turns.response_html:
The reason you're seeing ColorSync Utility is likely because it's the default "gatekeeper" for image and scanning profiles on macOS, but it rarely acts as the final destination for your files.

To find your scans, the "where" depends entirely on which software is actually pulling the data from the Brother printer. Here are the three most likely spots to check on your Mac Mini:

1. The Default "Pictures" or "Documents" Folders

Most Brother drivers (and macOS's native Image Capture) default to one of two places:

  • Pictures folder: Look for a subfolder named "ControlCenter" or just the root Pictures folder.
  • Documents folder: Check for a folder named "Scans".

2. AirPrint / "Printers & Scanners" Settings

If you are scanning directly from the System Settings, macOS usually defaults to the Desktop or Pictures. You can verify this by:

  1. Going to System Settings > Printers & Scanners.
  2. Selecting your Brother printer and clicking Open Scanner.
  3. In the scanning window, look for a dropdown menu labeled "Scan To:". This will show you exactly where the current session is sending files.

3. Brother iPrint&Scan / ControlCenter4

If you are using Brother's proprietary software:

  • iPrint&Scan: Open the app and click on Machine Settings or Scan Settings. It will list a "Save to" path.
  • ControlCenter: Check the Configuration tab under the "Scan" button you clicked. It usually lists a destination folder under "Target Directory."

Quick Tip for Finding "Lost" Scans

If you just finished a scan and can't find it, use Finder's "Recents" view or use Spotlight (Command + Space) and type kind:image or kind:pdf and sort by Date Created.

Would you like me to help you set up a specific "Scan" folder on your Mac Mini so they always go to the same place in the future?
